entry.title: Masters of Albion - Longplay Full Game Walkthrough [No Commentary] 4k

media:group.media:title: Masters of Albion - Longplay Full Game Walkthrough [No Commentary] 4k
media:group.media:description:
Masters of Albion is a unique god game created by Peter Molyneux and his team at 22 cans. It has many different elements of his past games mashed together. Lots of references to Fable. There is quite a bit good and a decent amount of jank or bad. It's very early access, I think it needs around 6 months to a year of work for the majority of people to enjoy this game.
I personally enjoyed most of my time with it, my favorite thing so far has been the tranquil music created by the one and only Russell Shaw. Some tracks in here are clearly inspired by his past work on Fable 1 and 2. I quite enjoyed the building system as well, deciding what to add to which plot to speed up resource growth or to decorate for your own pleasure. The day's are usually quite relaxing to build to and it encourages you to take your time exploring or building. I enjoyed cooking the food but I didn't like how vague the requests are for it at times. The voice acting was very well done and felt very reminiscent of the Fable games as well which I quite enjoyed.
A few negatives. First the performance is rough, especially later on with more enemies and people on screen. The Hero combat needs a lot of work it feels like it was just added a month before release. The nights are to brutal with spawning I feel like instead of it being unlimited spawns (most nights) I would prefer a set number dependent on the difficulty you choose at the start. Right now its far to overwhelming. If it stays this way turrets need a big buff or we need access to double or triple the amount found on the map naturally. Instead of taking plots from needed areas like more housing.
Another thing to add to this, I'd like more plots or be able to buy them. This is the driving part that kept me playing the most. More plots to decorate and speed up resource gathering would be better. Could unlock certain ones from doing quests for example unique structures like mansions, crypts, farms all accessible when you posses someone. That have fun Fable style quests behind them. Being able to explore the starting crypt later on would be cool as well. The Arena needs a massive nerf, without the Rubber Duck I'm unsure how you were supposed to beat it. It was the only time I thought to myself I might get soft locked if I keep trying to beat it since it costs Gold and Favors to compete. I think it's silly that it costs you anything at all... YOU BUILT IT & OWN IT! Last thing is the Hand Powers need to feel better right now they feel like a nothing burger.
Lots more I could say but I do enjoy the game I just hope they continue to keep updating and making it better. Like always I hope you enjoy this longplay :)

entry.title: Sacred 2: Fallen Angel - Longplay Full Game Walkthrough [No Commentary] 4k

media:group.media:title: Sacred 2: Fallen Angel - Longplay Full Game Walkthrough [No Commentary] 4k
media:group.media:description:
Sacred 2: Fallen Angel full game walkthrough as the Dryad. A fun game it can be a short or long journey depending how many quests you choose to do along the way. I chose to do many quests thus leading to a longer journey. The first 3 zones (Tyr Lysia, Artamark, and Nor Plat) are my favorite, they're also the zones I had the most fun exploring in, plus the music was great. I'd say The Swamp was probably my 4th favorite. Then it starts to drop off after that, I feel like most of the other zones are a little to linear or just not as fun to explore. It makes sense when you see how I spent 20 hours in the first 3 zones and 10 hours in the last 7 zones, with 3 of those hours dedicated to The Swamp. The worst zones (in my opinion) being Dyr Lain and Bengaresh. Dyr Lain was to linear, annoying to move through, also had annoying jumping plants. The Desert/ Bengaresh wasn't as bad, just empty (I mean it's a desert). Plus annoying teleporting enemies. The nice thing is you can blast through the zones you don't enjoy very quick, so if you don't enjoy them you can just go to the next.
I think my favorite things about Sacred 2 is the vast world, different enemy designs, the humor, the build diversity along with their respective classes and the unique mounts. There is a lot going on in this game and although it's not perfect, it is fun. I hope you enjoy this longplay.

Fallout: New Vegas longplay with commentary, this was quite the grand adventure. From Goodsprings to Primm, Novac to Boulder City, Freeside to the Strip. This was by far my favorite playthrough I've done of New Vegas thus far, I look forward to more adventures in these wastes whether they be a brand new adventure or maybe continuing where I left off. Till then, I hope you enjoy this longplay :)

entry.title: The Lord of the Rings: Adventure Card Game - Longplay Full Campaign Walkthrough [No Commentary] 4k

media:group.media:title: The Lord of the Rings: Adventure Card Game - Longplay Full Campaign Walkthrough [No Commentary] 4k
media:group.media:description:
The Lord of the Rings: Adventure Card Game, Full Campaign (Battle the Armies of Sauron). This game is based on the LOTR LCG and I found it to be quite fun, in fact I picked up the core set and a few expansions because of how great this was. I wish they made DLC for this game because I would 100% buy it... oh well at least there is a good amount of content for the asking price. Oh also some great voice acting and a very fitting soundtrack. *Coughs* The Prancing Pony / Tavern song. What surprised me the most about this game is just how fun Deck Building was, I spent a good amount of time theorizing what card to add to my deck or which card to remove. Overall a fun time if you enjoy Lord of the Rings, deck building, and card games. I hope you enjoy this longplay ;)

media:group.media:description:
Reanimal longplay full game walkthrough with commentary found all the coffins for the secret ending too. Tried to do a good amount of exploring but still missed quite a few masks sadly not sure how much concept art I missed but got a decent amount of them. The three things that really stood out to me were the great sound design, the disturbing creatures/monsters and overall tone of the game. Mixed together it was very fun to play and not to long or drawn out, well I hope ya enjoy watching this longplay.
Thanks to THQ Nordic for giving me a key.
